Clustered Observations: CR2 Bands and Gene Screening

Source: vignettes/vcmoe-clustered.Rmd
vcmoe-clustered.Rmd

Single-cell data are usually collected from a handful of donors, and cells from the same donor share unmeasured effects. When u is a donor-level quantity (for example the age or time point of each donor), all cells at a given u come from one or a few donors, so cell-level standard errors can be far too small. This tutorial goes from a fit to cluster-robust confidence bands and then to a screen of candidate genes, treating donors as independent clusters.

library(VCMoE)

Simulate donor-clustered counts

Twelve donors, each observed at its own time point u, contribute 80 cells. Cells belong to one of two latent components; marker shifts the component probability, and the response depends on signal with opposite signs in the two components. A donor effect enters every cell of that donor.

set.seed(1)
n_donor <- 12L
cells <- 80L
donor <- rep(seq_len(n_donor), each = cells)
u <- ((seq_len(n_donor) - 1) / (n_donor - 1))[donor]
n <- length(donor)
marker <- rnorm(n)
component <- ifelse(rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.3 + 1.8 * marker + 0.8 * u)) == 1, 1L, 2L)
signal <- rnorm(n)
library_size <- exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.3))
eta <- log(library_size) +
  ifelse(component == 1, 1 + 0.3 * u + 0.4 * signal, 0.2 - 0.5 * u - 0.2 * signal) +
  rnorm(n_donor, 0, 0.1)[donor]
dat <- data.frame(
  y = rnbinom(n, size = 6, mu = exp(eta)),
  log_library = log(library_size),
  u = u, donor = donor, marker = marker, signal = signal,
  noise1 = rnorm(n), noise2 = rnorm(n)
)

Fit the model and refine it

The null model for the screen contains the library-size offset in the experts and the component marker in the gating. Fitting one grid point per donor time point keeps every grid point supported by data. The theta ridge stabilises the dispersion when few cells carry a component.

fit <- vcmoe_fit(
  y ~ offset(log_library) | marker,
  data = dat, u = "u", k = 2L, family = "negative-binomial",
  bandwidth = 0.3, u_grid = sort(unique(dat$u)),
  control = list(seed = 3, n_starts = 2, maxit = 300,
                 negbin_theta_ridge = 0.05, negbin_theta_target = 8)
)
fit <- vcmoe_refine(fit, tol = 1e-9, maxit = 2000)
head(vcmoe_diagnostics(fit)[, c("u", "converged", "stop_reason", "objective_delta", "refined")])
#>                      u converged stop_reason objective_delta refined
#> 0           0.00000000      TRUE   tolerance    6.369944e-07    TRUE
#> 0.090909091 0.09090909      TRUE   tolerance    1.194968e-06    TRUE
#> 0.18181818  0.18181818      TRUE   tolerance    1.560205e-06    TRUE
#> 0.27272727  0.27272727      TRUE   tolerance    1.624012e-06    TRUE
#> 0.36363636  0.36363636      TRUE   tolerance    1.599456e-06    TRUE
#> 0.45454545  0.45454545      TRUE   tolerance    1.664505e-06    TRUE

vcmoe_refine() continues the local EM with a tight tolerance. The default stopping rule is relative, so with many cells it can stop before the local maximum; inference then often finds a sandwich bread that is not positive definite.

Cluster-robust bands and path tests

Passing the donor of every fitted row gives CR2 intervals with Bell-McCaffrey degrees of freedom and simultaneous bands from a wild cluster bootstrap. Path tests ask whether each coefficient function is zero or constant along u; path_sets adds a band over the interior grid points.

band <- vcmoe_confband(
  fit, cluster = dat$donor[fit$rows_used], type = "simultaneous",
  coefficient_set = c("expert", "gating"),
  control = list(multiplier_B = 999L, seed = 1, path_tests = TRUE,
                 path_sets = list(interior = 2:11))
)
band
#> VCMoE confidence bands
#>   family: negative-binomial
#>   components: 2
#>   engine: local_grid_em
#>   type: simultaneous
#>   covariance: CR2
#>   level: 0.95
#>   coverage theory: local_likelihood_asymptotic_with_bias_and_boundary_caveats
#>   interval rows ok: 96/96
head(band$intervals[, c("u", "parameter", "estimate", "se", "df", "lower", "upper", "status")])
#>   u                                                      parameter   estimate

#> 3 0                            expert:component1:(Intercept):slope  0.5511223

#> 5 0 gating_contrast:component1_vs_component2:(Intercept):intercept  0.9697666
#> 6 0      gating_contrast:component1_vs_component2:marker:intercept -1.9174393

band$tests[, c("parameter", "path_set", "zero_p_value", "constancy_p_value")]

With only twelve donors the function warns that the intervals are sensitivity analyses; band$diagnostics reports the active and effective number of donors at every grid point.

Screen candidate genes

vcmoe_gene_screen() asks, for each candidate, whether it is associated with the response within the components, given the fitted model. Candidates enter the gating as nuisance, so a gene that only marks the components is not flagged. A candidate that strongly marks the components can be listed in profile_genes, which refits its gating effect before testing.

X <- as.matrix(dat[fit$rows_used, c("signal", "noise1", "noise2")])
screen <- vcmoe_gene_screen(fit, X, cluster = dat$donor[fit$rows_used],
                            grids = 2:11, B = 999L, seed = 2)
screen
#> VCMoE gene screen
#>   candidates: 3 (profiled: 0)
#>   grid points: 10; clusters: 12; bootstrap draws: 999
#>   status ok: 3/3
#>   BH q <= 0.05: 1
screen$genes[, c("gene", "statistic", "p_value", "q_value", "argmax_component", "effect_per_sd", "status")]
#>     gene statistic p_value q_value argmax_component effect_per_sd status
#> 1 signal  6.339454   0.001  0.0030       component2    0.15932999     ok
#> 2 noise1  2.772646   0.271  0.4065       component2    0.10768978     ok
#> 3 noise2  2.124346   0.745  0.7450       component2    0.08123199     ok

signal is the only candidate with a within-component effect, and it is the only one with a small adjusted p-value. The screen tests associations on the log-mean scale of each expert; effect_per_sd gives the size of the strongest one per standard deviation of the candidate.
